The reachability sweep listed MorningBrief.tsx among 8 unreachable page files and it was DELETED — then the suite went red with ENOENT, because server/adminTruth.test.ts opens that component's SOURCE FILE BY PATH and asserts on its text (F25e: live requires online === true, undefined is its own state). A file can be consumed three ways — imported, referenced by symbol, or read by path — and both an import graph and a symbol grep miss the third. It was restored, and the standing question recorded then ('unmounted yet pinned by a truth guard: wire it or retire it WITH its guard, never silently') is what this diff answers. Wired, not deleted.  ONE DEFINITION, TWO CONSUMERS. The brief needs the urgent-lead count, which lived inline inside the 'Urgent leads' SummaryCard JSX. Passing it to the brief would have meant re-typing the predicate — !isCallbackDuplicateLead && ACTIVE_LEAD_STATUSES.has(status) && urgencyScore >= 4 — and a re-typed predicate is exactly how the weekly digest nearly drifted from the daily report on the lead count, which is why countActionableLeads became a shared function instead of two SQL predicates. Extracted to one `urgentLeadCount` useMemo that BOTH the card and the brief read, so the header cannot disagree with the page it introduces. The memo sits ABOVE the isLoading early return; `lint:hooks` (audit-hook-after-return) passes, which is the check that would have caught it otherwise.  DEGRADES BY DESIGN: the component self-suppresses when there is no real signal (no yesterday data -> 'Quiet start'; no overnight activity -> line skipped entirely), so a dead morning renders less, never a fabricated all-clear.  ─── ALSO IN THIS DIFF: the PII linter blind spot, closed and RED-GREEN PROVEN ─── lint-pii's console rule used `[^)]*`, which cannot span a closing paren, so ANY PII interpolation following a call on the same line was invisible. The leak that shipped past it: console.log(`inv ${String(p.invoiceId).padEnd(7)} "${p.name}" ... ${p.phone}`) — a full name AND a full phone — while the weaker sibling statement on the next line, with no inner call, was caught. The rule was scoring the easy half. Widened `[^)]*` -> `[^;]*`: reaches across parens, still stops at a statement boundary so a match cannot run away into an unrelated statement.  THE WIDENING SURFACED 8, AND THEY WERE NOT ALL REAL — 5 raw leaks and 3 already-masked diagnostics (`***${String(caller).slice(-4)}`). A gate that flags correct code is a gate the next person learns to ignore, so the rule now sets `maskable: true`, joining the convention the log-field rules already use via MASKED_VALUE_SIGNAL. The 5 real ones were fixed by REMOVING redundancy rather than blanket-masking: two lines already carried the invoice id (and one the alg_estimates id), so the customer name was duplicate identification and was dropped; two phone prints were reduced to last-4.  ONE WAIVER, AND IT NEEDED A MECHANISM. `backfill-invoice-phone-from-customer.mjs:233` prints two customer names side by side under the heading 'given-name misses (surname exists — inspect before trusting)'. Masking that field does not protect anyone; it prints two rows of asterisks and decides nothing. There was no line-level waiver in this linter — only value allowlists — so one was added: `// pii-allow: <reason>`, with the reason REQUIRED so an empty marker silences nothing. Waived by SIGNATURE, never by filename.  RED-GREEN, BOTH DIRECTIONS: planting the exact original blind-spot shape (a `.padEnd()` call before the PII) INSIDE the very file that carries the waiver turns the audit red and prints the planted line — proving simultaneously that the widened rule catches the class it was widened for, and that the waiver is line-scoped rather than quietly file-scoped, which is the property a file exclusion would have destroyed. Probe removed; audit back to `clean (780 files scanned)`.  EVIDENCE: tsc --noEmit 0 errors; lint:hooks 'no hook-after-early-return patterns detected'; lint:pii clean (780 files); full serial suite green including adminTruth.test.ts, the guard that caught the deletion.  NOT CLAIMED: no browser screenshot of /admin with the brief mounted, and no live morning has rendered it — the composition and its degradation paths are asserted by the component's existing guard, not by a dawn run. The operator authorised arming, but a read-only prod count taken first shows only 5 of 2,238 customer phone numbers carry an sms.opt_in row (0.2%), so arming would silence marketing SMS to 2,233 customers. Prior entry (andon ramp) superseded per the rolling-manifest rule.  ─── PRIOR DIFF, SUPERSEDED ─── WHAT THE OPERATOR SEES — the admin's red / amber / green finally read at the same brightness, and money columns stop going ragged. This is a VISIBLE change and the only one in the diff; the customer site is untouched.  ★ THE DEFECT, MEASURED FROM TAILWIND'S OWN TOKENS. Tailwind's palette is perceptually uniform WITHIN a hue and not ACROSS hues. At the shades this console actually uses — 1,881 occurrences across 52 distinct shades — its shipped OKLCH lightness reads: red-400 70.4%, emerald-400 76.5%, amber-400 82.8%; red-500 63.7%, emerald-500 69.6%, amber-500 76.9%. That is a 12.4-point lightness spread at ONE nominal step, running BACKWARDS: amber renders brightest, red dimmest. On a shop-floor andon board the colour meaning 'stop, money is at risk' was the quietest thing on the screen and 'caution' pulled the eye first. Equal step numbers were doing unequal work, and no component was wrong — the palette was.  THE FIX, AND WHY IT TOUCHES NO COMPONENT. Tailwind v4 compiles utilities to a var() lookup — verified in the shipped bundle: `.text-red-400{color:var(--color-red-400)}` — and custom properties inherit. So re-tinting the nine tokens on `.admin-shell` re-tints all 1,881 existing call sites at once, with zero component edits and zero sweep risk. Deleting the block restores stock Tailwind exactly; there is no migration to unwind. Scoped to the admin shell deliberately: the customer site keeps stock Tailwind, so no public page pixel moves.  CHROMA IS COMPUTED, NOT EYEBALLED. Each value sits inside its hue's maximum sRGB chroma at that tier's lightness, found by converting OKLCH -> Oklab -> linear sRGB and binary-searching the ceiling per hue. This matters because an out-of-gamut colour is silently clamped by the browser, and clamping shifts lightness — it would have reintroduced the exact drift being removed. The computation is also why the tiers sit at L 0.80 / 0.72 / 0.66 rather than higher: red's chroma ceiling COLLAPSES as lightness rises (0.191 at L70 down to 0.114 at L80), so equalising high would have bleached the one colour that must stay urgent. Red therefore keeps the most chroma at the text tier — severity now leads on saturation, which is a chosen signal, instead of on lightness, which was an accident.  TYPOGRAPHY: `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` on admin `table/th/td`. Proportional digits make a currency column ragged and make a figure jitter as it re-renders. Applied wholesale to admin tables rather than per-component because a grid where only some columns align is worse than one where none do; 28 files already used it ad hoc, so this makes the rule uniform instead of partial.  EVIDENCE: client/src/__tests__/andon-ramp.test.ts, 8 tests, all green. It asserts the MECHANISM, not the literals — every tier is equal-lightness, tiers descend soft->text->fill, every colour is inside sRGB (same conversion re-implemented in the test so a bad edit cannot pass), red holds the most chroma at the text tier, and the tabular-nums rule exists.
